description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three accuracy metrics: Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy. The x-axis, labeled Initial Confidence, has a linear scale, ranging from 0.87 to 1.00, with a tick label interval of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled Accuracy, also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.2, with a tick label interval of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Initial Accuracy in green with a dashed line and diamond markers, Final Accuracy in blue with a solid line and circle markers, and Δ Accuracy in orange with a dashed line and diamond markers. The Initial Accuracy line starts at approximately 0.7 and increases to around 1.14, showing a steady upward trend with some fluctuations. The Final Accuracy line begins at about 1.03 and rises to approximately 1.17, also exhibiting a generally increasing trend. The Δ Accuracy line starts at around 0.3 and ends at approximately 0.8, displaying a relatively stable trend with some minor fluctuations before a slight increase towards the end.
